findings.rationale: MD's uploaded updates are essentially zero in almost every round (median norm_ratio 0.008 against a federation median near 1, z=-10.8 after size adjustment; per-round norm_ratio is 0 in 14 of 20 rounds and never above 0.043). Its cosine to the median update is near zero (mean 0.02), i.e. no training signal. A client of its size (n_train 6683) should produce a large update, so this looks like the global model being returned without training. Its local performance is normal (AUC 0.824, CITL -0.004), so the fault is in the uploads rather than the data.

SC's updates are near zero in nearly every round (median norm_ratio 0.006, z=-7.3; norm_ratio 0 in most rounds and at most 0.146), with cosine near zero (mean 0.02). This is the same non-training signature as MD and OH, for a large client (n_train 3798). Local AUC (0.8225) and CITL (-0.017) are normal, so the data look fine and the fault is in the uploads.

OH's updates are near zero in almost every round (median norm_ratio 0.005, z=-8.2; norm_ratio 0 in most rounds, with cosine to the median averaging -0.03, z=-4.2). This matches the free-rider signature seen in MD and SC. Local performance is normal (AUC 0.8015, CITL -0.013), so the fault is in the uploads, not the labels or features.

report.summary: Screened all 52 clients with update, performance, drift, feature and subgroup views, then confirmed suspicions with narrower queries. Three clients (MD, SC, OH) show near-zero update norms and near-zero cosine to the consensus across nearly all 20 rounds, with normal local AUC and calibration. I report them as free riders from round 1. Other candidates did not hold up under confirmation: the AgeGroup subgroup outliers (MD, SC, OH) vanished or moved at higher epsilon, the MI drift spikes were scattered with no consistent onset, and the DC/SD/NH feature outliers were within noise at higher epsilon. No evidence of label noise, prevalence shift, poisoning, drift, missing-artefact, subgroup bias or explanation instability. Budget left: 1.0 epsilon.
